### 4. **Socrates** (c. 470–399 BCE)
Socrates was a classical Greek philosopher credited with laying the foundations for Western philosophy. ### 5. **Hippocrates** (c. 460 – c. 370 BCE)
Known as the "Father of Medicine," Hippocrates was a Greek physician who made substantial contributions to medicine and is the eponym of the Hippocratic Oath, a document that lays forth ethical guidelines for physicians.

Democritus was a pre-Socratic Greek philosopher and one of the first scientists in the modern sense. He was the originator of the idea that all matter was made up of atoms, contributing significantly to early atomic theory.

### 7. **Aeschylus** (c. 525/524 – c. 456/455 BCE)
